chia: Inverting a sequence of functions; time-memory-trade-off hardness (Beyond-Hellman) [AACKPR17]
proposed: Pebbling / labelling of an (e,d)-depth-robust DAG; sequential-recompute lower bound [DFKP15, ABH17]
what_gained: One well-studied primitive (a single DRG); the verifier reconstructs the graph bit-for-bit from pk
what_lost: Narrower foundation: security rests on one single-layer DRG's depth-robustness vs Chia's layered function-inversion hardness

chia: 7 tables (Beyond-Hellman nested 6x), 2^k entries each; plot phases forward-propagation -> backpropagation -> compression -> checkpoints
proposed: DRSample single-layer DRG (bucket-method back-edges); label l_i = H(pk||i||parent labels); Merkle-committed
what_gained: Far simpler plotting (one SHA-256 pass per label); data-independent, verifier-reproducible bit-for-bit from pk
what_lost: Single layer, no table compression; far less engineering maturity; no compressed on-disk format

chia: Time-memory-trade-off lower bound from the Beyond-Hellman layered-table construction [AACKPR17]
proposed: Asymptotic Omega(N/log N) depth-robustness [ABH17]; MEASURED back-cone phi ~= 0.49*N at thesis N (C1)
what_gained: A concrete, MEASURED space floor on the actual plot (not only an asymptotic claim)
what_lost: Bound is asymptotic + single-layer; measured phi extrapolated ~800x beyond the measured range, not re-proven at thesis N

chia: Partial-storage resisted by table design; no published recompute-vs-storage curve
proposed: keep 25% labels -> 12.99 s recompute, keep <=10% -> 60-81 s; honest ~tens of ms; phi saturates ~0.49 (C1)
what_gained: A measured trade-off curve that makes a usable response timeout delta possible
what_lost: Trade-off holds under the sequential model; an unlimited-core parallel attacker floor ~= 5.15 s (C1)

what_gained: Self-contained proof: opens a verifier-reconstructible DRG parent set + Merkle paths, no table lookups
what_lost: ~12x larger than Chia (256 B -> 3168 B) and grows LINEARLY in the DRG in-degree delta

chia: prover ~640 ms (slow-HDD quality lookup, 10 ms/seek); verifier near-instant, NO published ms
proposed: prover ~7 us; verifier ~17 us (in-RAM Merkle open) (C4)
what_gained: Seek-free, in-RAM proving -- prover ~5 orders of magnitude faster than Chia's disk lookup
what_lost: Assumes the plot is RAM/fast-readable; Chia is designed to tolerate a slow HDD

chia: ~300 s high-end (400 GiB RAM) up to ~6 h commodity; 101.4 GiB (k=32)
proposed: 164.8 s native floor (delta=2; up to 411 s at delta=8); 100 GiB labels (~200 GiB with Merkle tree) (C4)
what_gained: Comparable/faster native plot; one SHA-256 per label, no multi-phase compression
what_lost: Native-rate floor (pure-Python plotter ~33-55x slower); ~200 GiB on disk with the tree vs Chia's compressed 101.4 GiB

chia: Non-interactive: the challenge is broadcast from the blockchain at each signage point; the farmer self-checks its plot (no per-prover request)
proposed: Interactive: a peer challenges a peer over the DHT; the prover must answer within a response timeout delta
what_gained: No blockchain / timelord required; fits a live DHT where nodes already exchange RPCs every maintenance round
what_lost: Relies on an interactive liveness assumption and a wall-clock timeout delta that Chia avoids entirely

chia: N/A -- Chia has no response-timeout delta
proposed: false-reject ~0 for all delta>=1 s (honest p99 cross-region 146.5 ms); false-accept = 0 for delta<=2 s; delta=5 s marginal vs the 5.15 s parallel floor (C2)
what_gained: delta<=2 s cleanly separates honest from cheater under realistic network jitter
what_lost: Correctness hinges on a tuned delta and jitter assumptions; a loose delta (delta=10 s at delta_g=8 / keep-75%) admits a cheater (C2)

chia: N/A at the PoSpace layer -- soundness/identity is enforced by consensus, not per-node liveness challenges
proposed: rho<=20% labels -> caught by the 1st challenge (p_fail 0.89-0.97); evicted in 3 consecutive fails (MAX_FAILS); knee at rho~25% (C3)
what_gained: Cheap periodic challenges catch storage-cheaters quickly and evict them
what_lost: A cheater keeping >=33% labels escapes the delta=2 s timeout (but then stored ~75% of the tree); detection is recompute-time-bound, not coverage-bound

chia: Plot-grinding costly by construction; 'ungrindable trunk' (PoSpace+VDF only); identity enforced at consensus level
proposed: id=SHA256(pk) UNSALTED & attacker-chosen -> grindable in ~N hashes (targeted capture = const 2 plots, B2); per-identity cost x3.25e9 vs no admission (B5); BUT a minimum-plot-size check is MISSING (B5 gate FAIL)
what_gained: PoSpace raises the per-identity cost ~3.25e9x (33 B keypair -> 100 GiB plot) and rate-limits the NUMBER of identities
what_lost: Rate-limits identity count, not PLACEMENT -- the unsalted id is grindable; the Sybil-cost floor is CONDITIONAL on an unimplemented minimum-plot-size check
proposed_source: B2_targeted.csv (grind cost, 2 plots); B5_sybil.csv (3.25e9x, min-plot-size gate)

chia: Chained with a VDF ('Proof of Time', class-group repeated squaring by timelords) -> blockchain-grade consensus
proposed: Standalone PoSpace admission over the DHT; no VDF, no chain
what_gained: No timelord / VDF / blockchain dependency -- self-contained node admission
what_lost: No proof-of-elapsed-time or global ordering; cannot give the consensus-grade guarantees Chia's VDF provides
proposed_source: node/pospace_admission.py (standalone admission; no VDF in the design)

chia: Beyond-Hellman table format resists time-memory trade-offs [AACKPR17]; grinding-resistant trunk
proposed: DRG depth-robustness (no sub-linear retention, C1) + no-plot-amortisation: k identities need k distinct plots, distinct roots (B5 gate PASS); pk<->id binding blocks plot reuse (B5 gate PASS)
what_gained: Provably one plot per identity; a Sybil advertising another identity's commitment is rejected by challenge_peer (B5)
what_lost: Amortisation across challenges WITHIN one plot is not separately hardened; rests on the single DRG's depth-robustness
